description:
In this task, you will analyze the results of the Muncie unsteady flow simulation to determine velocity distributions across the river channel.

The simulation results are stored in the HDF5 file `Muncie.p04.hdf` (or `Muncie.p04.tmp.hdf`) located in the project directory `/home/ga/Documents/hec_ras_projects/Muncie/`. Your goal is to extract the velocity time-series data for ALL cross-sections, calculate statistics, and identify the location with the highest velocity.

**Requirements:**
1. Use Python (available in the terminal) to explore the HDF5 file structure and extract velocity data.
2. Create a CSV file at `/home/ga/Documents/hec_ras_results/velocity_distribution.csv` containing the following columns for every cross-section:
   - `cross_section`: The River Station identifier
   - `max_velocity`: The maximum velocity recorded at this location across all time steps
   - `mean_velocity`: The average velocity across all time steps
   - `min_velocity`: The minimum velocity across all time steps
3. Determine which cross-section has the absolute highest peak velocity.
4. Create a summary text file at `/home/ga/Documents/hec_ras_results/velocity_summary.txt`. The first line must contain the cross-section identifier, and the second line must contain the peak velocity value.

Note: The velocity data is typically located under `Results/Unsteady/Output/Output Blocks/Base Output/Unsteady Time Series/Cross Sections/` within the HDF5 file.
